Condemning All Involved in Spreading Personal Info and Undue Punishment

October 15, 2026 · Source: chat backup of the #✅ㅣ인증딱지 channel

This statement is based on a backup of the conversation in the Discord channel #✅ㅣ인증딱지. It sets out what the users imnyang and hyonsu did. The channel conversation covered runs from September 27 to October 13, 2026; replies received at other times and related material are included as references.

Source of the material: This conversation backup was made by din0_san, a participant in that channel. din0_san is named here with their consent. din0_san also took part in the conversation in this channel. So the conversation in this statement was not secretly viewed by an outsider. It is a record kept by one of the participants in the conversation.

Why this is being published: hyonsu is a moderator of the ADOFAI Community Server (ACS) and is also involved in modding-related work on the 7th Beat Games side. Decisions by someone in this position directly affect whether mod developers can continue their work and whether they can use the community. This statement asks for confirmation that those decisions and sanctions went through a fair process, and is published so that other mod developers and community members do not go through the same thing. It also records the personal information tracking by imnyang that happened along the way.

This statement was written to establish the facts, not as an emotional attack. To that end, the following principles were followed.

  • Every claim is accompanied by the original message, together with the surrounding context.
  • Remarks that could be read as jokes, remarks open to different interpretations, and private remarks unrelated to this matter are not covered.
  • People are named by their Discord username (ID). Nicknames that appear in the original conversation are explained in each chapter's “Slang and expressions” section.
  • Personal information of the affected person and of third parties (year of birth, area of residence, other account names) has been redacted.
  • Anything that cannot be confirmed from the record is marked “not confirmed”.

AI was used to structure the page, draft and edit the text, and produce this English translation. Quotes and chat logs are taken verbatim from the Discord backup file, and the Korean original was checked against the source by people. The English translation is machine-generated and has not been reviewed line by line.

A disclosure about ADORAP and TINU first — square3ang

There are signs that ADORAP was distributed externally while koren was developing it alone, so it was a project that may have conflicted with 7th Beat Games' policy. That distribution happened before I joined, but since I later became a contributor, I will not avoid responsibility for this project.

TINU started from a project (ADORAP) that koren had been working on personally before joining our team, an independent reimplementation of the original game. The team then took it over and turned it into a mod that runs on top of the original game. In other words, ADORAP and TINU come from the same project, and we said so publicly in the TINU distribution notice at 23:02 on October 13.

TINU is a project that was released before 7th Beat Games clarified its standards on clones. However, before its release koren had asked 7th Beat Games for permission to launch ADORAP and was told the review would take a while; at the time we read the ambiguous parts of the existing IP policy broadly and released TINU before receiving that answer, which was an oversight on our part (Chapter 1, Reference J). When I later reviewed it again, I judged that parts of it could conflict with 7th Beat Games' policy. So I took TINU down myself before 7th Beat Games reached a decision (including on modlist.org), and I told giacomo directly about this and the reasons.

Show details (earlier IP policy, how TINU worked, the 7th Beat Games reply)

For reference, the Making External Tools for the Editor section of the earlier 7th Beat Games IP policy (web archive record) prohibited tools that replace the game (please do not develop tools as a substitute for the game) and allowed tools that add on to the game (Add-ons are OK!). The section on clones for educational purposes (Cloning 7BG Games for Educational Purposes) allowed non-commercial clones for educational purposes, but prohibited distribution other than for demonstrations (Do not distribute clones except for performance presentations or demonstrations.). The clause explicitly prohibiting unapproved clones was added later.

The released TINU only worked as a MelonLoader mod inside an installed copy of A Dance of Fire and Ice. Game assets were extracted from the user's own game and encrypted with a key that only unlocks on that device. So it could not be used without the game or as a replacement for the game.

Later, in its reply, 7th Beat Games said that it thought highly of the new editor and timeline features, but that porting part of the game (the editor) to Rust goes beyond the purpose of modding and counts as a clone. It also said it would state in its IP policy that unapproved clones are not allowed (see Reference A in Chapter 1). Following this decision, I am rebuilding it in the direction 7th Beat Games recommended (a C# mod).

This statement does not claim that the projects above had no problems. Its purpose is to record the personal information tracking and the procedural problems that occurred along the way.

About my past controversies — square3ang

I too have been criticized in the past for failing to follow community rules and guidelines, and I do not deny that criticism. Those events, however, came before June 6, 2026, when hyonsu notified me in the name of 7th Beat Games that my mod developer permissions were restored (Chapter 1, Reference C), and this statement deals only with what happened after that.

Part 1. The Core Problems

1. An insider with moderation authority targeting a specific person

Subject: hyonsu

hyonsu, who acts as a 7th Beat Games insider, said an official policy was aimed at a specific person, and announced action in advance. They are on record as having received the original source code without the ADORAP developers' consent, and posted a list of gallery posts attacking square3ang while assessing the community trolling as a “success”.

Facts

  1. hyonsu called 7th Beat Games' guidelines and reply our guideline and our reply. They also spoke as a 7bg insider, mentioning access to the 7bg repository, announcements of modding guideline changes, and handling bans. In June 2026, they directly informed square3ang, in the name of 7th Beat Games, that their mod developer permission was being restored (Reference C).
  2. On October 13 at 21:24, they posted a screen of the upcoming modding guidelines with the Modding is limited to PC only clause highlighted. They then wrote 정사각형저격함 수고하세요(“sniped square3ang” “take care”) and 폰에디터만들지말라고 막은거임(“blocked it so they won't make a phone editor”). This is a remark to the effect that an official policy was made with a specific person in mind.
  3. Earlier the same day at 21:21, they said 가이드라인변경이있었는데(“there was a guideline change”), posted a screen with another upcoming clause, Do not feed anything from 7BG into AI (e.g., porting the game code…), highlighted, and wrote koren 차단함 수고(“blocked koren” “take care”). koren is one of the ADORAP developers. The earlier 7th Beat Games IP policy (web archive record) already had wording in the Making External Tools for the Editor section saying it did not support public distribution of tools that reproduce the game's mechanics as they are. However, that section concluded with please do not develop tools as a substitute for the game. Add-ons are OK!, so what it blocked was tools that replace the game, and it allowed tools that add on to the game. The same policy also had a section on clones for educational purposes (Cloning 7BG Games for Educational Purposes), which allowed non-commercial clones for educational purposes but prohibited distribution other than for demonstrations. The new clause (Cloning 7BG Games) that explicitly prohibits unapproved clones and adds AI-related wording came later. hyonsu introduced this new clause as if it targeted a specific developer, saying koren 차단함(“blocked koren”).
  4. From 21:56 to 22:00, asked when the punishment would happen, they replied giacomo깨어나면 몇개좀물어보고(“when giacomo wakes up, I'll ask them a few things”). They then said 정사각형은이미 두번째목숨이기때문에 답변안받고 한거면 담궈도됨(“square3ang is already on their second life, so if they did it without getting a reply, we can deal with them”).
  5. All ADORAP developers banned. Afterward, in ACS, not only square3ang but also kkitut, kyulio and koren, who were listed on ADORAP, were banned. However, the four people's degree of involvement differs. There are signs that koren distributed it externally while developing it alone. kkitut only took part in development and was not involved in distribution. kyulio's name became known when the repository Contributors capture posted by Participant L went straight into imnyang's draft report email (Chapter 4). Of the four, square3ang, kkitut and koren also took part in developing TINU. Even so, the four initially received the same action regardless of their degree of involvement. As the reply to the appeal (below) confirms, the actual target of the bans was TINU. TINU continues from ADORAP, and square3ang's side first said so publicly in the TINU distribution notice at 23:02 on October 13 (see the introduction). Meanwhile, imnyang had already said at 05:40 on October 10, three days earlier, TINU랑 ADORAP이랑 코드 베이스 똑같음(“TINU and ADORAP have the same codebase anyway”). The ban notices all four received gave the same reason, 7BG 가이드라인을 악의적으로 회피한 프로그램 배포(“distributing a program that maliciously evaded the 7BG guidelines”), and the action was a permanent ban. Since TINU was also distributed in ACS, there is no disagreement that ACS could act on this matter. Also, that ADORAP itself had potential policy problems is as stated in the introduction; what is discussed below is the action on TINU, the actual target of the bans. However, measured against the ACS moderation punishment guidelines in force at the time (revised October 4, 2026) and the server rules, the level, procedure and stated reason of the action raise the following problems. First, the applicable clause and the level. In the guidelines, the penalty for providing, distributing or developing a mod that violates the Modding Rules & Guidelines is 경고 2(“2 warnings”) (2-7-3). Yet in its reply to the appeal, ACS said TINU is a game clone, not a mod, so it falls under copyright infringement rather than the modding guidelines (below). In that case the relevant clause is sharing copyright-infringing content, for which the penalty is 1 warning, with discretionary punishment when intent is recognized (2-8-1). ACS treated this in its reply as an attempt to circumvent, that is, as intentional. However, 7th Beat Games, which ruled TINU a clone, called TINU a gray area and said it did not separately judge personal motives such as whether the developers tried to evade the guidelines (Reference I). No basis for judging intent came from 7th Beat Games' replies either. Also, the clause explicitly banning unapproved clones was added after TINU was released (see the introduction). The earlier policy's educational-clone section did already prohibit distribution beyond demonstrations, but whether TINU counted as such a clone was something 7th Beat Games itself decided only after discussion. Under either clause, a permanent ban for a case where whether there was a violation at all is open to dispute is far heavier than the guidelines' base level. For reference, square3ang already had 2 earlier warnings, so 2 more warnings would amount to a permanent mute under the cumulative standard. The later adjustment to a permanent mute (below) matches that standard. Second, the procedure. Under the server rules, a discretionary punishment is decided at a staff meeting and the reason is passed on to the person. Whether a staff meeting took place cannot be confirmed from outside. What can be confirmed is that the notice contained only the one line above, and a detailed explanation came only after square3ang appealed (below). Third, the reason. The act named in the reason was distribution, but kkitut and kyulio did not take part in distribution. In particular, kyulio is not among the TINU repository's commit authors (Reference K). In the ADORAP repository too, kyulio has only one commit, from September 16, and even that was later reverted (Reference L). Even if, as imnyang said, the two projects share a code base, it is hard to say kyulio contributed to the TINU code, so the ban is hard to explain even by the “team-wide action against all TINU development participants” that ACS gave in its reply. On October 13, hyonsu posted a capture of their own message written to the 7th Beat Games side. In it, hyonsu asked how 7th Beat Games had replied to the DM in which square3ang's side asked 7th Beat Games for permission for a Rust port, saying for ACS process, and wrote that having asked for permission at all meant they knew it was not covered by the guidelines, calling it a bigger problem. A private inquiry in which square3ang's side asked 7th Beat Games for permission was being sought as grounds for the ACS process. However, 7th Beat Games later replied that it was not involved in the ACS action and first heard of the bans from square3ang (Reference I).The appeal and the replies. On October 15, square3ang appealed through an ACS ticket (Reference H). ACS replied: (1) TINU is a game clone, not a mod, so it falls under copyright infringement rather than the modding guidelines. (2) It was judged malicious because the TINU developers had asked 7BG for permission to develop a Rust port, but before receiving a reply made and distributed it in a form that did not look standalone, which was judged an attempt to circumvent. (3) The project was treated as a team, so action was taken against every member who took part in development, and having only taken part in development is not grounds for lifting the ban. (4) Managing the mod developer role is not ACS's responsibility. ACS added that the bans are unrelated to 7BG and recommended not making further inquiries to 7BG. ACS later accepted square3ang's request and adjusted square3ang's punishment from a permanent ban to a permanent mute.The same day, 7th Beat Games (giacomo) answered square3ang's questions (Reference I): 7BG made no decision about ACS actions and only told ACS that it was not allowing the mods, and first heard of the bans from square3ang. TINU was a gray area but was ruled a clone after discussion. Personal motives, such as whether the developers tried to evade the guidelines, were not really discussed. 7BG has no opinion on moderation decisions about specific users in community servers.Putting the two replies side by side shows the following. First, 7th Beat Games, which ruled TINU a clone, did not judge personal motives, yet ACS gave malicious evasion as the reason for the action. Second, the ground ACS gave (distributing before receiving a reply) is also how 7th Beat Games saw it. giacomo too said that koren asked about launching ADORAP, was told the review would take a while, and that TINU was launched days later without waiting for an answer (Reference J). But 7th Beat Games gave this only as a reason for not restoring access to its own mod developer server, and said it was not involved in the ACS action. The person on record linking this ground to ACS punishment before the action is hyonsu, an ACS staff member. On October 13 hyonsu said in the channel 답변안받고 한거면 담궈도됨(“if they did it without getting an answer, we can punish them”), and wrote to the 7th Beat Games side without waiting our reply. Third, the reason first announced was distribution, but in the reply the explanation changed to action against the whole team. Neither the ACS rules nor the punishment guidelines contain any provision on team-wide punishment. Fourth, ACS said managing the mod developer role is not its responsibility. In fact, square3ang's access to the mod developer server (Reference D) was removed by 7th Beat Games, separately from the ACS ban. 7th Beat Games said it removed the access as a preventive measure while discussing TINU, and would not restore it for the time being in view of past history, including square3ang trying to get mod permission with a new account after mod access on ADOFAI.gg was removed (Reference J).
  6. On October 13 at 20:31, when a TINU update came up, they said TINU 곧뒤질예정이라(“TINU is going to die soon anyway”), mentioning the outcome of the action in advance.
  7. On October 10, when imnyang said a repository could be taken down with a DMCA, hyonsu asked about its effect and added 고소(“lawsuit”). The same day from 05:39 to 05:45, when Participant L, a former ADORAP team member, said 내컴퓨터에 논수정원본 있음(“I have the unmodified original on my computer”), imnyang suggested 정현수한테 보내보기(“try sending it to hyonsu”).     On the objection that “hyonsu is a 7th Beat Games insider, so it was fine for them to receive it”

    1. Even if there was a right, this was not a proper channel. Even assuming 7th Beat Games can assert rights over ADORAP, there were separate official channels a rights holder could use: contacting the developers directly (like the reply in Reference A), a DMCA notice, or legal proceedings. imnyang themselves mentioned a DMCA early that same morning. This source was not received through any of those channels.
    2. It was not a request from 7th Beat Games. The handover began in a private channel when imnyang suggested 정현수한테 보내보기(“try sending it to hyonsu”). Even Participant L, who sent it, did not know whether this code would be shared 7bg내에(“inside 7bg”).
    3. The sender had no right to pass it on. Participant L was a former team member who had left the team, and the source was a copy left on Participant L's computer. The other developers did not consent to this handover.
    4. imnyang, who suggested the handover, also knew it was a problem. imnyang refused to receive the same code themselves, saying 문제가 될수도 있음(“it could be a problem”). Yet they suggested sending it to hyonsu.
    5. The recipient had already decided on the action. At 05:20–05:23, about 15 minutes before receiving the source, hyonsu said 불법모드가아님 불법프로그램(“it's not an illegal mod” “it's an illegal program”), and while counting who the developers were (정끼코(“square-kki-ko”) / 4명임?(“four of them?”)) asked [별칭 가림]임?(“is it [nickname redacted]?”) 담궈?(“should we deal with them?”). This is a person who had already made up their mind receiving private material of the people subject to the action outside any official process, and it is hard to see as an objective investigation.
  8. On October 11 from 20:44 to 20:46, hyonsu posted screens of the A Dance of Fire and Ice gallery to the channel. The last capture is a list of posts from 18:16 to 19:02. When another participant gave inquiries like 저 왜 밴됐어요?(“why was I banned?”) as an example, they replied 그런 티켓은 내가 담당하고 있음(“I handle those tickets”), and then wrote 갤에서 고로시하는것도 내가 담당하고 있음(“burying people on the gallery is also my job”). Whether this remark reflects actual activity, or was a joke or exaggeration, cannot be told from the record alone. Regardless of actual activity, this statement takes issue with an ACS staff member making such a remark at all. On June 17, hyonsu also posted a notice in the ACS announcements channel about moving mod developer applications. In ACS, hyonsu has the Server Admin, Server Moderator and Staff roles together with the 7th Beat Games role (Reference F). That is, hyonsu is a staff member with ACS moderation authority.
  10. Point that needs to be confirmed: an admin screen leaked outside. The 18:32 post 「트집잡아서 처벌한건지는」(“Whether they were punished over a nitpick”) (A Dance of Fire and Ice gallery No. 44602, archive) in the list hyonsu posted has 5 captures of the ACS #모드 channel attached (Reference E). In these captures, a Discord timeout icon is visible right next to the names of square3ang (server nickname “good opencode man”) and kyulio. This icon next to a nickname is visible only from accounts with server moderation authority. That is, the screen of someone with ACS moderation authority was used in an anonymous post attacking square3ang. hyonsu is one of the ACS staff members with that moderation authority (item above, Reference F). For reference, the 18:43 post in the same list, 「정사각형 병신맞고 잘 처벌했는데 뭐가문제?」(“square3ang really is a moron and was rightly punished, so what's the problem?”), the comment on post No. 44602 (얼붕이1), and the comment (얼붕이1) in another capture hyonsu posted to the channel the same evening are all shown with the leading IP digits 119.197. This statement does not identify the poster from the circumstances above. Several people have ACS moderation authority, and the first two parts of an IP shown by DCInside are shared by many users of the same carrier, so matching leading digits alone do not show that they are the same person. However, how an admin screen came to be used in an outside anonymous post is something the ACS staff can check internally, so we ask them to check it (see Requests).

References (material outside the channel backup)

Caveats A rights holder responding to an unauthorized port can in itself be legitimate. What this chapter takes issue with is not whether there was a response, but the procedural fairness of an insider naming a specific person in a private conversation and announcing the outcome in advance. The 7th Beat Games reply in Reference A did not mention sanctions. Yet a permanent ban (Reference B) was later issued in ACS. How the remarks in Chapter 1 connect to this ban needs to be confirmed by the staff. In the October 11 gallery matter, which of the posts in the list hyonsu wrote cannot be identified from this material alone. What can be confirmed is only that hyonsu posted the list writing 커뮤니티분탕치기대성공(“community trolling, huge success”), and did not deny it when asked whether it was them. Nicknames of unrelated users in the gallery captures have been redacted. The extent of kkitut's and kyulio's involvement in distribution and development, and square3ang's number of earlier warnings, are as stated by square3ang's side.
Slang and expressions
정사각형 → square3ang
Korean nickname for square3ang. They are called by this name in the original conversation.
정현수 → hyonsu
hyonsu's display name.
토끼 → Bunny / the bunny
Nickname for kkitut (literally “bunny”).
스퀘어 → square3ang
A way of referring to square3ang (“square”).
코리아 → Korea (Koren)
A way of referring to koren (literally “Korea”).
정끼코 → Jungkkiko
Abbreviation made from the first syllables of 정사각형 (square3ang), 끼툿 (kkitut) and 코렌 (koren).
얼불춤 → ADOFAI
Abbreviation of A Dance of Fire and Ice (ADOFAI).
칠비지 → 7bg
“7bg” read out in Korean; 7th Beat Games.
지아코모 → Giacomo
giacomo written in Korean.
7bg → 7th Beat Games
7th Beat Games. Developer of A Dance of Fire and Ice (ADOFAI).
ACS → ADOFAI Community Server
ADOFAI Community Server. The ADOFAI community Discord server.
giacomo → giacomo
A 7th Beat Games representative.
분탕 → trolling
Deliberately disrupting a community; trolling.
갤 → gallery
A DCInside gallery. Here, the A Dance of Fire and Ice gallery.
칼춤 → wielding the knife
Literally “sword dance”; a moderator handing out sanctions freely.
고로시 → taking people out
Slang from the Japanese ‘殺し’ (killing). Here it means ganging up on a specific person on the gallery to bury them.
티켓 → ticket
A channel on a Discord server for sending private inquiries to the staff.
저격 → took a shot at
Targeting a specific person to attack or criticize them.
담궈도됨 → we can take them down
“담그다” is slang for scolding or dealing with someone. Means “it is fine to punish (them)”.
두번째목숨 → second life
Means that since they have already been sanctioned once, this is their last chance.
쳐맞아야 → should get smacked
Vulgar form of “should get hit”. Means they should be sanctioned.
곧뒤질예정 → about to die
“뒤지다” is slang for “to die”. Means it is about to disappear (be removed) soon.
차단함 → blocked
Means “blocked”. Here it is used to mean that the new guideline clause blocked that developer's work.
리버싱 → reversing
Reverse engineering. Taking a finished program apart to figure out its structure or code.
DMCA → DMCA
A takedown request under US copyright law (Digital Millennium Copyright Act).
레포 → repo
Repository.
감상 → browsing / admiring
Literally “appreciating”; here a light way of saying freely opening and viewing someone else's code.
모드 개발자 권한 → mod developer role
Mod developer permission; a role given to verified mod developers in the official community.

2. Personal information tracking of square3ang

Subject: imnyang

For about 40 minutes, imnyang looked for square3ang's personal information and other accounts and shared them in the channel.

Facts

  1. On October 13 at 22:06, imnyang posted a capture of a wiki article about square3ang. At 22:11 they revealed another user's (예노갓) year of birth, and at 22:13 they posted a capture of square3ang's location information (this location information had been public on square3ang's Steam profile). The harm of the personal information tracking was not limited to square3ang alone.
  2. They then wrote 뒷조사를 선호하진 않지만 조금만 둘러봐야지(“I don't like background digging, but I'll look around just a little”) (22:16) and 뭔가 개인정보가 나올거 같은 기분이(“I have a feeling some personal info is going to turn up”) (22:23). They went ahead knowing themselves that it was “background digging”.
  3. From 22:31 to 22:35, they wrote 무엇을 현실에서 하고 다닐지는 알거 같음(“I think I can tell what they do in real life”) and 스팀 친구가 다 멀리있냐(“are all their Steam friends far away?”), and went as far as checking their Steam friends list. The Steam friends list is also information visible on a public profile, but imnyang used it to guess at square3ang's real-life activities.
  4. At 22:38, they downloaded square3ang's repository (launcherlzma), extracted the commit author names and emails with git log, and posted the result. This result identified another account of square3ang's.
  5. When square3ang made their GitHub repositories private and blocked imnyang, imnyang wrote 정사각형 나 차단했는데?(“square3ang blocked me?”) and 내부 고발자 있네 확신함(“there's a whistleblower” “I'm sure of it”).
  6. At 22:46 they wrote 이래서 내가 항상 이런거 안하는 건데 오늘 너무 화났음(“this is why I never do this kind of thing, but I was so angry today”), and at 23:07 they admitted their wrongdoing, writing 근데 이거 내가 잘못한 거 맞음 사과드립니다.(“but yeah, I was wrong about this” “I apologize.”).
Caveats The location information and the Steam friends list were public information (items 1 and 3). What this chapter takes issue with is not whether each piece of information was public, but the act of gathering information from several places as “background digging”, sharing it in the channel, and even identifying another account through repository commit information. The 23:07 apology was made inside the channel, and the record does not show whether it reached square3ang themselves. The year of birth (예노갓), area, other account names and the 4 related captures have been redacted in this statement.
Slang and expressions
정사각형 → square3ang
Korean nickname for square3ang. They are called by this name in the original conversation.
정현수 → hyonsu
hyonsu's display name.
암냥 → Imnyang
A way of referring to imnyang.
칠비지 → 7bg
“7bg” read out in Korean; 7th Beat Games.
7bg → 7th Beat Games
7th Beat Games. Developer of A Dance of Fire and Ice (ADOFAI).
깃헙 → GitHub
GitHub.
Private → private
Switching a repository to private.
내부 고발자 → whistleblower
Whistleblower. Here it refers to the person who told the target that they were digging up personal information.

3. Disparagement of square3ang and mockery using their real name

Subject: imnyang

When imnyang disagreed with square3ang, they disparaged them in the channel, and when square3ang was timed out, they mocked them using their real name.

Facts

  1. On September 28 from 00:03 to 00:07, right after disagreeing with square3ang about the originality of a benchmark graph, imnyang wrote in the channel 사람이 미친거야 저건(“that person is crazy”) / 이상한 사람한테 트집 잡혔어(“I got nitpicked by a weird person”), and 난 쟤 대응하기 싫어 이상한 머저리야(“I don't want to deal with them” “they's a weird idiot”).
  2. At 00:32, replying to imnyang's 이상한 사람한테(“by a weird person”) message, hyonsu posted a screen showing square3ang had been timed out for 3 days and said 이유는잘모르겠지만타임아웃된듯(“not sure why, but looks like they got timed out”).
  3. The same day at 12:14, when imnyang asked 왜당한거야(“why did that happen to them?”), Participant L replied 그 분은 니가 찔렀다고 생각 중임(“they think you snitched”) (square3ang thinks imnyang reported them). In response, at 13:24 imnyang replied using square3ang's real name: [본명 가림]게이불쌍하노(“poor [real name redacted] guy”).
  4. At 13:46, din0_san replied to this message asking 뭐야 걔 이름 어케앎?(“what, how do you know their name?”) and said 아 인스타에 있구나(“oh, it's on Instagram”). Then at 14:55, imnyang posted a capture of square3ang's Instagram profile screen (real name, 6 followers, 8 following) and wrote 얘 친구 없냐?(“does this guy have no friends?”). They found square3ang's Instagram account, confirmed their real name, and shared that screen in the channel to mock them.
Caveats The real name appears to have been written in the name field of square3ang's Instagram profile. The record does not show how imnyang found that profile (search method). The real name in the capture has been redacted in this statement. Who applied the timeout and for what reason also cannot be confirmed from this material alone.
Slang and expressions
게이 → -dude / the guy
Internet community slang meaning roughly “the guy who…”. Here it is attached after a real name to mock them.
찔렀다 → snitched
Slang for “reported (someone)”.
머저리 → moron
A derogatory word for a foolish person.

Part 2. Background and the Double Standard

4. Remarks about reversing ADORAP, to which they had no access

Subject: imnyang

imnyang said they had reversed ADORAP, to which they had no access, and learned how it worked inside, and said TINU was an exception when it came to taking mods apart.

Facts

  1. On October 10, when another user said of imnyang 얘는 접근권한이 태초부터 없었음(“they never had access from the very start”), imnyang replied ADORAP 리버싱해서 이미 알만큼 앎(“I reversed ADORAP, so I already know as much as I need to”). This is their own statement that they reversed it without the developers' permission or access rights.
  2. On October 13, in response to the point that taking apart a competing mod is not a good thing, they replied 난 모드 안뜯어봄 사용함 TINU는 약간 예외임(“I don't take mods apart, I use them. TINU is a bit of an exception.”). This reads as meaning that TINU was the one they did take apart.
  3. For reference, the draft report email imnyang wrote on September 27 to send to giacomo says I’m not sure exactly how it was implemented or whether any original code or assets were used. The first draft at 19:08 listed only Kkitut. At 19:09, Participant L posted a capture of the ADORAP repository's Contributors list (kkorenn, square3ang, Kkitut, kyulio), and the second draft at 19:44 included the GitHub accounts of these 4 people as they were. In the conversation at the time of the report (September 27), there is no remark about knowing ADORAP's internals. They first said ADORAP 리버싱해서 이미 알만큼 앎(“I reversed ADORAP, so I already know as much as I need to”) on October 10. The record does not show when they actually reversed it.
Caveats What they reversed and how does not appear in the conversation. It is confirmed only by their own remarks, and there is no physical evidence.

Reverse engineering. Taking a finished program apart to figure out its structure or code.

5. A report that started from personal feelings

Subject: imnyang

The motive for the report that imnyang stated was personal feelings, and they also showed resentment toward a competing project.

Facts

  1. On September 27 from 18:59 to 19:00, when Participant L said they had an ADORAP build because they had access to the repository, imnyang said of Participant L [별칭 가림]은 NDA에 휘말릴거야(“[nickname redacted] will get caught up in an NDA”) and DCMA 에 휘말릴거야(“will get caught up in a DCMA”). Separately, from 19:00 to 19:01 they said 저거 7bg에 난 보낼거임(“I'm going to send that to 7bg”), giving as the reason 나의 심기를 건듦(“it got on my nerves”), and to someone trying to stop them they said 나 막지 마셈 나는 보낼거임(“don't stop me, I'm sending it”). At 19:03 they added 내 앞에서 불법적으로 만든 도구 가지고 나랑 비교한다? 는 참지 못함(“comparing me, in front of me, to a tool made illegally? I can't stand that”). From the flow of the conversation, the “tool made illegally” imnyang refers to here is ADORAP.
  2. On October 10 they said 글로벌쪽에서 ADOFAIRenderer가 내 사용자 다 빼가던데(“on the global side, ADOFAIRenderer was taking all my users”). ADOFAI Renderer is a project square3ang started in 2024 (based on the release notice in the public mod list) and control_delta took over on October 27, 2025.
Caveats The report itself was in the form of a polite inquiry, and anyone has the right to report. This chapter is meant to record the motive for the report and the context that the same person went on to the personal information tracking in Chapter 2.

6. A double standard around OrbitRender

Subject: imnyang

imnyang said they had reverse engineered the release of the competing mod ADOFAI Renderer and tried to have Codex analyze and bring in its strengths. In the same period, they drafted a report email about ADORAP over its internal implementation and legality, and called it 불법적으로 만든 도구 (“a tool made illegally”).

Facts

  1. Name. The OrbitRender repository was created on September 13, 2026 under the name imnyang/ADOFAIRenderer. That address now redirects to OrbitRender. The release files for public releases 0.11.8–1.2.0 were also ADOFAIRenderer.zip. square3ang's ADOFAI Renderer started in 2024, and there is an alpha build from January 2025. After square3ang stepped away, control_delta took it over on October 27, 2025 with a notice that the project was restarting, and it was later handed over to AEF.
  2. OrbitRender's first release on September 17 also came out under the name ADOFAIRenderer. The same day, when control_delta told them ADOFAI Renderer had started as an alpha in 2024, imnyang said 뭐 제가 후발주자니까 제쪽에서 이름을 바꾸긴 해야할거 같아요(“well, since I'm the latecomer, I think I should be the one to change the name”) and said they would rename it to OrbitRender. About 2024 they replied 그땐 얼불춤에 관심이 없었습니다(“back then I wasn't interested in ADOFAI”) (Reference G). On October 13, about a different person's render mod that used the same name, separate from ADOFAI Renderer, they said 이것도 AdofaiRenderer 던데 고소당할듯(“this one is also AdofaiRenderer, they'll probably get sued”).
  3. Reverse engineering the ADOFAI Renderer release. On September 27 at 20:10, imnyang posted a screen opening the release file ADOFAIRenderer_0.3.2-BETA.zip (Mods/ADOFAIRenderer.dll, UserLibs) of ADOFAI Renderer and wrote 에셋번들의 폐헤(“the downside of asset bundles”). Then, in what appears to be a decompiler, they expanded the list of resources included in ADOFAIRenderer.dll (ADOFAIRenderer.Bundle.Win64/OSX/Linux.*) and the referenced assemblies (FFmpeg.AutoGen, MelonLoader), and said 나는 리버스 엔지니어링 해봤음 이 모드(“I've reverse engineered this mod”). This conversation took place on the very day imnyang wrote the draft email reporting the ADORAP developers to 7th Beat Games (Chapter 4).
  4. Attempt to analyze and port ADOFAI Renderer using Codex. On September 29 from 23:46 to 23:54, imnyang posted captures of ADOFAI Renderer's FFmpeg processing code and examined its structure. 18 minutes later, on September 30 at 00:12, they wrote codex한테 경쟁사의 장점을 분석하고 도입해보라고 했는데 성능이 회귀함(“I told codex to analyze the competitor's strengths and bring them in, but performance regressed”). At the time, the only render mods were OrbitRender and ADOFAI Renderer.
  5. Why this attempt is a problem. On September 27 imnyang said of the release of the competing mod ADOFAI Renderer 리버스 엔지니어링 해봤음(“I've reverse engineered it”), and on September 30 wrote that they had told Codex to analyze the competitor's strengths and bring them in. On that same September 27, imnyang wrote a draft report email saying they did not know how ADORAP was implemented (Chapter 4), and criticized the same ADORAP as being 불법적으로 만든 도구 가지고(“a tool made illegally”) (Chapter 5). The projects involved are different, but since they themselves took apart someone else's release and tried to take its strengths, while reporting the other side's project over its internal implementation and legality, this can be seen as a double standard.
  6. In the same conversation, imnyang said 모드리스트가 내가 배꼈다는 이유 알거 같음 걔네가 릴리즈만 안했지 내가 만든 기능을 예전부터 구현은 하고 있었음(“I think I get why the mod list says I copied. They just hadn't released it, but they had been implementing the features I made for a long time.”). Where plagiarism had been pointed out, imnyang themselves said the other side had been implementing the same features first.
  7. On October 13 they also examined competing mods. After posting a MelonLoader log at 20:51, at 20:52 they said 근데 이건 ADOFAIRenderer 이슈 아니냐?(“but isn't this an ADOFAIRenderer issue?”), and at 20:53 and 20:55 they posted screens of ADOFAI Renderer's mod list entry and its render settings. Then from 20:56 to 20:58 they said 스크롤하는데 왜 저렇게 맵이 움직이는거야(“why does the map move like that when scrolling”) and 랜더 Startup 타임 왜이리 느림 뭘 하길래(“why is the render startup time so slow, what is it doing”), and when another participant mentioned an FFmpeg build, they said 얘네는 내부적으로 무슨 밴치를 했길래 자기네들이 더 우월하다고 생각하는걸까(“what kind of benchmark did they run internally to think they are superior”). At 22:01 they said 내 경쟁 모드는 패치를 어떻게 하길래(“how does my competing mod do its patching”). The 20:56–20:58 remarks came right after they had named ADOFAI Renderer and posted its screens. The 22:01 remark does not name the mod, but given this context from the same day it appears to refer to ADOFAI Renderer. In between, at 21:05, opening another render mod that included its source (the separate same-named project above), they said GitHub을 볼 수 없는 환경에서도 마음대로 코드 감상 가능(“you can browse the code freely even where you can't see GitHub”).

References (material outside the channel backup)

Caveats This chapter does not claim a license violation or code theft. Since ADOFAI Renderer's source is public, viewing or decompiling it in itself is hard to see as illegal. What this chapter takes issue with is the double standard of reporting only the other side over the same kind of act. For reference, ADOFAI Renderer was MIT licensed up to 0.3.2, imnyang knew this (September 29 conversation), and OrbitRender has no attribution. However, whether code was actually carried over has not been confirmed. From the words 성능이 회귀함(“performance regressed”), it reads as having been applied at least once, but whether it remained in the final release is unknown.
Slang and expressions
얼불춤 → ADOFAI
Abbreviation of A Dance of Fire and Ice (ADOFAI).
7bg → 7th Beat Games
7th Beat Games. Developer of A Dance of Fire and Ice (ADOFAI).
갤 → gallery
A DCInside gallery. Here, the A Dance of Fire and Ice gallery.
뜯어 → take apart
Taking a program apart to look at its internal code (decompiling and analyzing).
리버스 엔지니어링 → reverse engineering
Taking a finished program apart to figure out its structure or code.
폐헤 → downside (typo)
A typo for “폐해” (harm, downside).
밴치 → bench (typo)
A typo for “벤치” (benchmark, performance measurement).
감상 → browsing / admiring
Literally “appreciating”; here a light way of saying freely opening and viewing someone else's code.
경쟁사 → competitor
Literally “competitor company”; here, another competing mod (and its developer).
회귀 → regression
Regression; performance getting worse than before.

Requests

  1. To imnyangWe kindly ask that you delete the personal information about square3ang that you collected and shared (the wiki and location captures, commit author information, and account links), and take care that those who received it do not spread it further. We would also hope that the apology you made in the private channel is delivered directly to the person concerned.
  2. To 7th Beat Games and the ADOFAI Community Server staffWe ask that you review hyonsu's remarks, made in their insider position, explaining policy by pointing to a specific person and announcing action in advance, and look into whether there was a conflict of interest. We also request that you look into how a screen visible only to ACS moderators came to be used in an outside anonymous post attacking square3ang (Chapter 1, Reference E).
  3. To the ADOFAI Community Server staffsquare3ang's punishment was adjusted to a permanent mute after the appeal, and we consider this a level consistent with the guidelines. However, we would ask you to look again at the punishments of the other three. A punishment for distribution does not fit kkitut, who did not take part in distribution, or kyulio, who did not take part in developing TINU either; and even for koren, who did take part in distribution, we consider a permanent ban far too heavy in light of the guidelines' penalty levels. Taking into account the problems with the level, procedure and stated reason of the action (Chapter 1), we ask that you review the three punishments in light of the guidelines.
  4. To hyonsu and the former ADORAP team member who passed on the source code (Participant L)We ask that you both destroy the ADORAP original source code that was said to have been passed to hyonsu on October 10 without the developers' consent, and, if it was shared with others or used elsewhere, disclose the purpose and circumstances.
  5. On the reporting and sanction process as a wholeWe ask that the process be reviewed so that the private motives and private conversations of people in a competitive relationship do not affect sanctions.
  6. To 7th Beat GamesWhen the modding rules or the IP policy are revised, please clearly state from when the rules apply. If no effective date is stated, they can be used retroactively as grounds for action against projects released before the revision. Also, when considering a revision to a clause, please fully review whether it could be seen as targeting a specific person or project, and whom it could actually affect and how. This request is based on an insider saying of the clause, right after this revision, 정사각형저격함(“sniped square3ang”) (Chapter 1). We would also ask you to confirm whether the ADORAP original source code that a former ADORAP team member (Participant L) said they passed to hyonsu on October 10 (item 4) was passed inside the company, and whether the source code was received through an official process.
  7. On OrbitRenderWe ask that you respect the source released under GPL-3.0 and the rights of its contributors, and that, if code from other projects was referenced or ported, you state its source and license.

If there are factual errors in this statement, please let us know with evidence. As soon as they are confirmed, we will revise the content to correct them and publish the revision history as well.

A Request to Readers

The purpose of this statement is not to attack anyone. Its purpose is to keep the same thing from happening again to other mod developers.

Please do not use this statement as an excuse to harass the people mentioned or look for their personal information.

Also, right after the events of Chapter 2, imnyang wrote 내부 고발자 있네 확신함(“there's a whistleblower” “I'm sure of it”). We ask the community to watch together so that the person who provided this record, and the people who were in the conversation, do not face disadvantages such as bans, loss of permissions or background checks because of this statement.
